subject: Materials Science
title: Drug-Eluting Stents
description: Learn Drug-Eluting Stents in one minute.

hook.text: A bare metal stent opens a blocked artery — but 30% clog again within a year. Adding a drug coating cuts that to 5%.

buildup.text: Drug-eluting stents are coated with a polymer layer containing antiproliferative drugs like sirolimus or paclitaxel.

discovery.text: The drug inhibits smooth muscle cell growth — preventing the neointimal hyperplasia that reclogs the artery.

twist.text: The polymer coating can trigger late thrombosis — blood clots forming months after implantation when the drug runs out.

climax.text: Biodegradable coatings dissolve after drug delivery — leaving bare metal that endothelializes normally.

punchline.text: A stent healing the artery it holds open — material, drug, and biology as one.

quiz.question: Why are biodegradable polymer coatings preferred on drug-eluting stents?
options: They make the stent cheaper to manufacture
They dissolve after drug delivery, reducing late thrombosis risk
They make the stent expand more easily
